Cinematic photorealistic photograph, vertical 9:16 portrait framing, shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, natural film-like color grade, realistic textures. Any animated characters present are rendered as glossy vinyl designer toys with smooth shiny plastic shading, physically integrated into the live-action scene with matched lighting, soft reflections and true contact shadows, live-action hybrid family-film look. Focal subjects composed centrally with generous headroom above and below for the vertical frame. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks. The scene is the settled group-photo moment of the backyard birthday party at dusk, framed to match a close-knit group photo: young adult friends in their 20s and 30s kneel and stand shoulder to shoulder in a tight cluster, all turned to face the camera and smiling, red plastic party cups in several hands, one friend holding a phone up with its flash catching mid-pop as if snapping a selfie of the group. Warm string lights are strung overhead between a leafy hedge and a wooden privacy fence behind the group, with a peaked house roofline just visible at the upper edge of frame. STARRY — a tall golden five-pointed star character with a friendly cartoon face on the star body, large cartoon eyes with white sclera and blue irises, thin black eyebrows, a happy open smile, wearing a pink polka-dot cone party hat, with rainbow-checkered fabric arms and legs, puffy white four-fingered cartoon gloves, and round shiny golden boots — stands centered at the back of the group, both puffy white gloves thrown high overhead in a triumphant wave, visible between the friends' heads and shoulders. The three CRASHERS — small toddler-sized creatures whose bodies are simple ROUND hooded onesies, soft round hooded baby-suit silhouettes, NOT shaped like bolts or diamonds or splats, the patterns only the FABRIC PRINT of each onesie: one onesie in orange fabric with a yellow zigzag print, one in blue fabric with a purple diamond print, one in green fabric with a multicolor paint-splatter print, each with a pale round face peeking out of its snug hood, big sparkly jewel-like eyes, rosy round blush cheeks, a tiny happy smile, and a red-and-white striped cone party hat on top of the hood — kneel and sit in a row at the very front of the group, arms raised and open in an excited wave, facing the camera. In the immediate foreground a rustic wooden picnic table holds bowls of tortilla chips, a squeeze bottle of mustard, and red party cups. But unlike a calm photo, the air is COMPLETELY FULL of colorful confetti frozen mid-fall: thick, dense confetti fills the frame at every depth, from high overhead near the string lights and tree canopy, drifting past and between the friends' faces and shoulders, swirling around Starry's raised arms and between the Crashers in front, all the way down to the immediate foreground in front of the lens; the ground beneath everyone's feet and the entire tabletop in the foreground are carpeted in a thick blanket of fallen confetti, with just as much still suspended motionless in the air at every distance from the camera to the fence behind, as if time froze mid-blizzard.
Throughout the ENTIRE shot there are EXACTLY three Crasher mascots in total (one orange zigzag, one blue diamond, one green paint-splatter) and EXACTLY one star mascot in total — the same four characters from the first frame to the last; no additional, duplicate, background, distant or partial mascots ever appear anywhere in the frame at any moment. Every human being in the scene is a young adult in their 20s or 30s — absolutely no human children, no babies, no toddlers, no minors, no middle-aged people, no elderly people, nobody with gray hair, no small human figures of any kind anywhere in frame or background; the only child-sized figures allowed are the three vinyl-toy Crasher mascots in their hooded onesies.
